- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- If model shows gradual upward trend (e.g., +0.1–0.3 per day) but true outcome spikes sharply, reduce forecast slope after spike; avoid overcommitting to continuation.
- When true outcome exceeds model by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, apply mean reversion: next forecast = previous true + 0.5×(true - model) to dampen overconfidence.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and model is rising, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent high to avoid “false optimism”.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period spikes (especially after 20–25 days); add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast from day 20 onward if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If model is flat or slightly declining but true outcome rises >1.5% from day 10 onward, assume momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.05–0.10 per day starting from day 10.
